.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 115 PM EST Sunday...

1. Seasonable and unsettled weather is expected through the 
first half of this week with rounds of showers.

2. Unsettled weather is expected to continue late next week 
into the weekend, with temperatures trending cooler this weekend. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 115 PM EST Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A dry afternoon is expected today as low pressure shifts 
eastward into the Canadian Maritimes, and high pressure over the 
Mississippi River Valley builds into the northeastern U.S. 
Seasonable temperatures currently in the mid 40s to lower 50s are 
expected to fall as we head into the overnight hours, dropping to 
the mid 30s to lower 40s by early Monday morning, which is 
relatively mild for this time of year. West-northwesterly winds will 
decrease into the overnight as well, though westerly gusts may 
continue at higher elevations with a modest low level jet overhead. 
Precipitation chances also increase again this evening and tonight 
as we remain under the influence of a large upper level low rotating 
over eastern Canada. The first shortwave it sends our way will move 
overhead tonight and Monday. Much like our recent round of 
precipitation, most of the shower activity will fall as rain, with 
some light snow possible across the higher terrain and portions of 
the Adirondacks/Northeast Kingdom, especially tonight. Any snow 
accumulation will be minimal below 2500 ft. Rain will be the name of 
the game on Monday with highs in the 40s and lower 50s again. 
Precipitation amounts are expected to be up to 0.20" at most, 
highest in the northern Greens. Winds could also be slightly breezy 
again Monday out of the northwest, but not overly impactful. After 
brief ridging Monday night and lows in the mid 20s to mid 30s, the 
next shortwave should strike on Tuesday, though precipitation 
amounts are expected to be lighter, up to 0.15" at most. Once again, 
Tuesday's seasonable highs in the upper 40s to mid 50s will limit 
much snow during the day, then overnight lows in the upper 20s and 
30s could allow for some light snow at higher elevations and cold 
spots. Tuesday's winds will be out of the southwest and slightly 
breezy, but again not overly impactful. On Wednesday, we'll be 
drying out with highs in the 40s to mid 50s and winds out of the 
west-northwest again.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A period of unsettled weather looks to continue late 
next week into the weekend, with additional chances for 
precipitation expected. A lage-scale trough is expected to develop 
across the eastern CONUS, with a developing surface low centered 
over the Ohio Valley, with a strengthening secondary low expected to 
develop and move through the Mid-Atlantic towards the New England 
Coast. Temperatures look to trend colder towards the weekend, with 
highs only in the 30s and low 40s. Model guidance continues to 
struggle with the expected low track, which will greatly influence 
how much precipitation northern New York and Vermont can expect, as 
well as precipitation type. Guidance is still rather split on whether 
the low will be suppressed far enough south that we miss out or if it 
will bring widespread precipitation to the region, but trends 
generally support a wetter solution although there is still even 
more uncertainty regarding the expected precipitation type. The 
latest guidance supports the higher terrain seeing their first 
significant snowfall of the season, while valley locations may 
remain as all rain this weekend. With this system still several days 
out, model outcomes are likely to change, with details becoming 
clearer over the next few days.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 18Z Monday...After a morning of IFR ceilings and reduced
flight conditions, all terminals have gradually been improving to
MVFR and VFR, with most locations expected to have a period of VFR
ceilings late this afternoon into the evening. Between 00Z and 06Z,
conditions are expected to trend back towards MVFR as the next round
of showers approach the region. Ceilings are expected to lower
between 1500 and 2500 ft AGL for the most part, although there is
some potential for even lower ceilings and possible IFR conditions
at KSLK. MVFR conditions are expected to prevail through the
remainder of the forecast period. Winds this afternoon have been a
bit variable in direction, generally west to northwesterly,
generally between 3 to 10 knots with occasional gusts in excess of
15 knots. Winds are expected to be light and variable overnight
before increasing out of the northwest tomorrow morning.

Outlook...

Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Veterans Day: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. NO SIG WX.
Thursday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight
chance SN.
Friday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance RA,
Slight chance SN.
